overview.description: Page One is a traditional Japanese card game that combines follow-suit trick-taking mechanics with a shedding objective. Players must follow the led suit or draw from the stock until they find a playable card. The game is known for its mandatory 'Page One!' declaration when a player is down to their final card, with failure to declare resulting in a severe five-card penalty.

history.origins: Developed in Japan during the 1950s and 1960s, it predates the 'American' Crazy Eights variant that often shares its name.
timeline: 1950s: Game actively played in Japanese social and student circles.
1970s: American Page One (Crazy Eights variant) gains popularity.
Present: Remains a staple of Japanese household and family card gaming culture.
history.evolution: The game evolved from trick-taking games into a unique shedding format requiring players to follow suit or suffer inflation.
history.cultural: The 'Page One' call is a ritualized declaration indicating the player has reached the final page of their hand.

setup.players: Typically four players sit in a circle; play and dealing proceed in a clockwise direction.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack with one added Joker. Rank: Joker > Ace > King > Queen > Jack > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 6 > 5 > 4 > 3 > 2.
setup.equipment: One standard pack of cards, one Joker, and a playing surface for the central trick pile.
setup.dealing: The dealer distributes four cards to each player one at a time. The remaining cards form the face-down stock.

rules.objective: Be the first player to successfully shed all cards from your hand by playing them to the central pile.
rules.gameplay: 1. Lead: Dealer's left leads any card to start the trick. 2. Follow: Players must follow suit if they hold a card of that suit. 3. Draw: If unable to follow suit, draw one-by-one until a playable card is found. 4. Joker: Can be played anytime to win the trick; if led, the next player sets the suit. 5. Next: Winner of the trick leads the next one. 6. Page One!: Call 'Page One!' when down to one card.
keyRules: Must follow the led suit if a playable card is held in the hand.
If unable to follow suit, players must draw from the stock until a card of the led suit or Joker is obtained.
The Joker always wins the trick; if led, the next card determines the suit for all following players.
Players must declare 'Page One!' when playing their second-to-last card to avoid a five-card draw penalty.
The first player to empty their hand of all cards wins the round immediately.

strategy.basic: Keep high cards to win tricks and gain the lead, allowing you to play suits your opponents might not have.
strategy.intermediate: Track which suits have been drawn from the stock to identify which players are likely to draw more cards.
strategy.advanced: Save the Joker for your second-to-last or last play to guarantee a win and exit the game safely.
tips: Lead suits that have appeared frequently to force opponents to draw from the stock.
Always be prepared to declare 'Page One!' the instant you play your second-to-last card.
In a 5-6 player game, the stock depletes quickly; be mindful of the reshuffle rules.

list.name: Five-Card Start
list.description: Players start with five cards each instead of four to extend the length of the game deal.

list.name: Restricted Joker
list.description: The Joker can only be played if the player has no cards of the led suit in their hand.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only restricts when the Joker may be played; no engine constant overrides are needed for this rule.

list.name: No Joker Last
list.description: Players are not permitted to win the game by playing the Joker as their final card.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rule is enforced by game logic; no engine numeric or config overrides apply to this variant.

difficulty.easy: Plays legal cards without strategy and frequently forgets to declare Page One, taking many penalties.
difficulty.medium: Consistently follows suit and uses the Joker strategically to win tricks and regain the lead.
difficulty.hard: Tracks drawn suits and played cards to maximize opponent draws while optimizing their own exit strategy.

considerations: Prioritizing follow-suit actions over drawing from the stock pile.
Strategic use of the Joker to secure the lead for subsequent tricks.
Monitoring the Page One declaration state for all players at the table.

ante.reason: Traditional Japanese Page One is a shedding game and does not utilize an ante or betting mechanism.

deal.description: Deal four cards to each player one at a time in clockwise order; remaining cards form the face-down stock.
deal.constraints: Dealer only; performed once at start of the game.

reveal_market.reason: This game does not feature a market zone or any market-based card acquisition mechanics.

buy_market.reason: There is no system for purchasing cards from a market in the traditional Page One ruleset.

buy_stock.reason: Players draw from the stock as a penalty or requirement rather than purchasing cards with currency.

fold.reason: The game requires players to continue until their hand is empty; folding is not a valid action.

check.reason: Betting rounds and the check action are not included in the traditional Japanese Page One game.

call.reason: Standard betting calls are not used in this follow-suit shedding card game.

bet.reason: Initial betting or wagering is not a component of the Page One shedding game loop.

raise.reason: As there is no initial betting, raising the stakes is not an applicable mechanic in this game.

declare.reason: Card combinations are not declared for points; see the Page One declaration for the shedding state.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private and are only revealed card-by-card as they are played to the trick pile.

award_pot.reason: There is no central pot of chips or currency to award at the end of the game round.

play_card.description: Play a card from your hand into the current trick pile on the table.
play_card.constraints: Must follow the suit of the lead card if possible; Joker may be played anytime.

draw.reason: The standard draw action is replaced by the draw_until_playable requirement when unable to follow suit.

discard.reason: Cards are played into a trick-taking format rather than being discarded into a common waste pile.

pass.reason: Passing is not permitted; players must either play a card or draw until a playable card is found.

bid.reason: Japanese Page One does not include an auction or bidding phase to determine a declarer or trump.

meld.reason: There are no melding or set-matching mechanics where cards are laid down in combinations for scoring.

go_out.description: Play the final card from your hand to win the current game deal.
go_out.constraints: Must have only one card remaining and have correctly declared Page One to the other players.
go_out.reason: This is the terminal winning action when a player successfully sheds all cards from their hand.

drawSources.notes: Must draw until a playable card is obtained from the pile.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: The winner of the previous trick leads any card to start the next trick.

wildcards.restrictions: Always wins the trick; if led, the next player determines the required suit for the trick.

validPlays.notes: Must follow the suit led or play the Joker to win the trick.

shedding.burnRules: Completed tricks are shuffled to form a new stock when the stock pile is fully exhausted.

edgeCases.text: When the Joker is led, the second player plays any card and that card sets the suit requirement.
Failing to say 'Page One!' when down to one card results in a mandatory five-card penalty draw.

customActions.description: Draw cards from the stock pile one-by-one until you obtain a card of the led suit or the Joker.
customActions.constraints: Only used if the player has no cards of the led suit in their hand at the time.
customActions.reason: This is the core requirement when a player cannot follow suit in the Japanese Page One game.

customActions.description: Verbally declare 'Page One!' to notify opponents that you have reached your final card in hand.
customActions.constraints: Must be performed immediately when playing your second-to-last card or winning a trick with it.
customActions.reason: This is a mandatory social declaration required to avoid significant card penalties during the shedding process.

hero.tagline: Follow suit, survive the draw, and declare your way to victory.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Japanese shedding game where you must follow suit or draw until you can. Call 'Page One!' on your last card or take a five-card penalty.

prompts.human: How do I play Page One?
prompts.ai: Page One is a Japanese shedding game. Follow the led suit if you can; if not, draw until you get a playable card. Don't forget to say 'Page One!' when you're down to your last card, or you'll have to draw five penalty cards.

scoring.description: None; the first player to shed all cards wins the round immediately.
scoring.winCondition: Shed all cards from your hand before any other player in the game.

penalties.missing_declaration: Mandatory five card penalty draw from the face-down stock pile.
